correctness.rationale: The finite model explicitly lists the thirty edges of the icosahedron, and two algorithmically distinct acyclicity predicates agree over all 4096 vertex subsets. The face vector, 984 augmented faces, 472 disjoint vertex-toggle matching pairs, 3984 covering relations, and complete acyclicity of the reversed Hasse arrows are independently checked by the executable certificate. Removing the empty-face pair leaves exactly one critical vertex and forty critical four-cells, proving an integral wedge of forty four-spheres by discrete Morse theory. Ordinary boundary ranks over F2 and F3 confirm all Betti numbers but do not substitute for the integral homotopy proof. The graph triangulation and its connected face-dual give the 120-element upper bound on the automorphism group; explicit generators realize all 120. Signed fixed-simplex Lefschetz traces are enumerated for all 120 and exact A5 character inner products reconstruct both antipodal constituents. The certificate was executed successfully and its output captured.

value.rationale: This is the canonical twelve-vertex icosahedral test case of the natural, literature-defined induced-forest/feedback-vertex-set simplicial invariant, outside the previously classified easy graph families. Determining the integral homotopy type of a nonpure five-dimensional complex with forty four-dimensional sphere summands is a meaningful complete classification. Computing the full rational A5 times C2 homology representation, with a nontrivial 15/25 antipodal split and no rotational invariants, provides structure inaccessible from Euler characteristic or Betti numbers. The exact scope is motivated and finite, not an arbitrary parameter slice; no sweeping generalization is claimed.
